summary: A GitHub issue (#834) in the ros2/rviz repository, opened by user trishmapow on Feb 28, 2022, reports that rviz2 running under ROS 2 Foxy on WSL Ubuntu 20.04 shows an empty grey area instead of the 3D grid, and publishing pointcloud data displays nothing. The reporter notes rviz2 works on a dedicated Linux laptop and that Rviz1 works on WSL Ubuntu 18.04 on the same machine; setting LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=true works without acceleration. The note also includes a long rviz2 startup log showing the OGRE 1.12.1 and GL renderer details, with the GL renderer reported as D3D12 (Intel Iris Xe Graphics).
one_line: GitHub issue #834 in ros2/rviz: rviz2 on ROS 2 Foxy under WSL and Docker shows an empty grey area instead of the 3D grid.
key_facts: GitHub issue #834 in the ros2/rviz repository was titled 'Empty grey area instead of 3D grid with rviz2 on WSL & Docker'.
The issue was opened by user trishmapow on Feb 28, 2022.
The issue carries the label 'backlog' and was open at the time of capture with 7 comments.
The reporter runs ROS 2 foxy on WSL Ubuntu 20.04 using precompiled packages.
Running rviz2 shows an empty grey area where the 3D grid should be, and publishing e.g. pointcloud data displays nothing.
Setting export LIBGL_ALWAYS_INDIRECT=0 and launching rviz2 through an Xrdp session did not fix the problem.
Setting export LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=true works without acceleration.
The rviz2 build is reported as RViz version Alpha compiled against Qt 5.12.8, with OGRE version 1.12.1 (Rhagorthua).
The reporter's host is Windows 11 Pro 21H2 (22000.493) with WSL kernel 5.10.60.1 and Intel Iris Xe graphics driver 30.0.100.9864.
Rviz2 works fine on the reporter's dedicated Linux laptop.
Rviz1 works fine on WSL Ubuntu 18.04 on the same computer.
The log shows GL_VENDOR as Microsoft Corporation and GL_RENDERER as 'D3D12 (Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics)'.
The log reports GL_VERSION 3.1.0.0 and 'OpenGl version: 3.1 (GLSL 1.4)'.
The CPU is an 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1165G7 @ 2.80GHz.
